partnershipPlan: Two patient partners who have had home antibiotics review the interview guide and the plain-language summary; an agency nurse lead comments on the complication definitions; results are discussed with the agency before publication.
socialListening: No social media listening; anonymised complaints and compliments about the OPAT service from the last two years are read for mentions of lines.

items.theme: Not wanting to be a nuisance
items.quote: Composite paraphrase: The arm had been tight for two days but I did not ring because I thought they would take me back in.
items.implication: Explore delayed reporting in interviews and make same-day advice easy to reach.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: They gave us a sheet about flushing, and I was frightened every time I pushed the syringe.
items.implication: Test demonstration teaching for carers who flush lines.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Half my week is fixing lines that would have come back to you if we had not been there.
items.implication: Seek agency notes so home-managed problems are counted.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: When a line stops at nine at night there is nobody at the hospital who knows the patient.
items.implication: Include out-of-hours escalation in the interview guide and the joint display.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: We choose midlines to avoid infections and then replace them twice in a six-week course.
items.implication: Report premature removal alongside infection when comparing line types.

summary: Five composite voices on delayed reporting, teaching, hidden work, escalation and line choice.
